explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM evaluation against human evaluation for both summarization and perspective extraction tasks, reporting Pearson correlation for summarization and percentage agreement for perspective extraction

prompts.notes: Paper mentions specific criteria for summarization evaluation (e.g., distinctness, overlap, relevance) but full prompts are not shown verbatim in main text; perspective extraction prompts are detailed in Appendix B

guidelines.notes: Human annotators scored summaries using criteria 1-5 from GPT-4 evaluation prompt (excluding format criteria) on 0-2 scale per criterion, resulting in total score from 0-10; for perspective extraction, annotators determined entailment vs non-entailment

sample_size.notes: 50 random samples from Perspectrumx for summarization validation; 100 random samples for perspective extraction validation

quantitative_scores.notes: Human scores tended to be lower than GPT-4 scores, suggesting GPT-4 might overestimate performance
Consistency between GPT-4 and first human annotator
Consistency between GPT-4 and second human annotator

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 scores show positive correlation with human evaluation (Pearson r=0.70 for summarization, 83-86% agreement for perspective extraction), demonstrating effectiveness as an evaluator despite some overestimation.

criteria_mapping.notes: Human evaluation used same criteria 1-5 as GPT-4 evaluation but excluded format-related criteria; both methods evaluated overall summary quality and perspective entailment
